Article Title: Govt asks Air India to ‘take responsibility’, tells DGCA to improve dope checks
Article Text:
The anger stems from the fact that AI 2379 may have narrowly avoided a disaster

Dope test changes

NEW DELHI: Govt has warned Air India to improve its oversight on operations and “take responsibility” for ensuring safety. The aviation ministry has also ordered DGCA to quickly revise its drug-testing rules and increase the percentage of personnel who must undergo mandatory testing.The govt has also directed the aviation regulator to enforce tougher penalties against those testing positive for “real” drugs, while giving additional chances to those whose positive results stem from medicines.The pilot-in-command of Air India’s badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi flight with 145 people onboard is learnt to have told investigators he had been prescribed sleeping pills due to personal problems which, he claims, led to the positive dope tests. His onboard behaviour is also underthe scanner after the cabin crew complained against him.“The final report of AI’s last June Ahmedabad crash in which 260 people lost their lives is not yet out and then something like this happens with Air India. Govt has taken a very serious view of what happened on AI 2379 and heads will roll. Aviation secretary Samir Sinha has told the AI brass in clear terms that the airline needs to take responsibility and that people found guilty by the probe will not be spared,” said a person familiar with the discussions.The anger stems from the fact that AI 2379 may have narrowly avoided a disaster. While cruising near Odisha, the aircraft reportedly got a series of warnings — many in quick succession — related to the three hydraulics systems, doors and elevator (which makes an aircraft ascend and descend). Autopilot had also tripped off. It had suffered a loss of altitude during cruise, injuring many on board.An Airbus team is in India to examine the reported issues along with officials of the French aviation regulator, with Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau probing whether these warnings were real or spurious and what had caused them. Pilots want Airbus to give a detailed explanation of the same.“Taking pilot-in-command’s alleged state and the multiple warnings, we compliment the co-pilot for ensuring the aircraft landed safely. This incident will lead to multiple changes to strengthen safety,” said a senior govt official.Many pilots feel the warnings “should have been” false as there was no way an aircraft suffering multiple whammies could have flown uneventfully for about two hours to land safely at its destination instead of the crew opting to land at the nearest airport.Senior pilots say there is a problem with the DGCA’s civil aviation requirement on the subject titled “procedure for examination of the aviation personnel for consumption of psychoactive substances” as it treats crew members testing positive due to taking some medicines the same as those who are addicted to “real” drugs or take them recreationally.
Article Summary: The pilot-in-command of Air India’s badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi flight with 145 people onboard is learnt to have told investigators he had been prescribed sleeping pills due to personal problems. The govt has also directed the aviation regulator to enforce tougher penalties against those testing positive for “real” drugs.

Article Title: Ready for long debate, can answer any question but opposition doesn’t want it: Amit Shah
Article Text:
Shah said govt had nothing to hide over an issue his rivals have used to attack him.

BJP

accuses Rahul of ‘anti-democracy, anarchic’ mindset

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Home minister Amit Shah on Wednesday flung a challenge at the opposition for a comprehensive debate over police action during the anti-NEET protests in Delhi on July 20, saying he was ready for a 24-hour-long debate in Parliament at an hour’s notice over their charge of police excesses against protesting students. He said govt had nothing to hide over an issue his rivals have used to attack him.“If they give their consent for discussion to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla at 2 pm, a debate can begin at 3 pm and go on till 3 pm the next day. I am ready to answer any question. But they (opposition) do not want debate to take place in Parliament. Let the people decide who is running away,” he told the media a day before the end of the monsoon session, which has been marred by the opposition’s disruptions over a host of issues. Soon after, parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said govt could even push for the session’s extension if the opposition wants.Shah said while the opposition had initially demanded his statement, govt had gone beyond it by agreeing to an extensive debate followed by his reply so that people could decide who was right and who was wrong.Amit Shah’s aggressive counter was seconded by a host of senior BJP functionaries, with party president Nitin Nabin saying the conduct of Rahul and the entire opposition was reflective of their “anarchic and anti-democracy” mindset.“The entire session is about to be over but they did not agree to a serious discussion over any issue,” he said, accusing them of running away after govt’s offer of a debate.With INDIA bloc MPs frequently accusing him of “running away” from Parliament, Shah hit back and said he was regularly in his chamber in the House. When the opposition was not letting the House function, what was the point of him going there, he asked.Expressing anguish at his opponents’ jibes like “lapata” (missing) and “bhagora” (fugitive) for him, Shah said these terms were being used only recently in parliamentary discourse.The minister later wrote to the Speaker, urging him to reach out to the opposition so that a discussion could begin. “You can allot as much time you think appropriate with mutual agreement. I want to participate in the discussion and I’m ready to answer every question of the opposition,” he said, adding that a solution to any issue in democracy emerged from dialogue and discussion.Congress had normalised disruption in Parliament, he said, adding a party which governed India for decades had fallen to such a low that it did not want discussion in the House.
Article Summary: Amit Shah said govt had nothing to hide over an issue his rivals have used to attack him. He said if they give their consent for discussion to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla at 2 pm, a debate can begin at 3 pm and go on till 3 pm the next day.

Article Title: Justice Yashwant Varma cash-at-home row: Can Parliament still remove judge from office?
Article Text:
. Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: There is little chance of the Lok Sabha continuing with Justice Varma’s removal motion despite the inquiry committee finding the charges relating to discovery of unaccounted currency notes in his official residential premises proved.As per Article 217(1) of the Constitution, a judge ceases to hold office if he/she resigns by sending a resignation letter written “under his hand addressed to the President”. Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings, finding the writing on the wall.How does a resignation of a constitutional court judge take effect? This question was answered by a five-judge bench of the SC in the Gopal Chandra Misra case on Feb 15, 1978. It was unanimous that once the judge sends his resignation to the President, he/she is deemed to have ceased to be a judge.In that case, the judge had set a prospective date for his resignation taking effect and before the arrival of the appointed date, he had withdrawn his resignation. SC had by four to one majority ruled that since the resignation was prospective, the judge had every right to withdraw it prior to the appointed date.
Article Summary: Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings. As per Article 217(1) of the Constitution, a judge ceases to hold office if he/she resigns by sending a resignation letter written “under his hand addressed to the President’

Article Title: 'Has no shame': Kangana Ranaut attacks Rahul Gandhi over Amit Shah debate row, Parliament logjam
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: BJP MP Kangana Ranaut on Wednesday launched a sharp attack on Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi over the continuing stalemate in Parliament, accusing him of making a "mockery" of the House and the country while refusing the government's offer for a debate on the students' protest.Ranaut alleged that Gandhi was demanding a statement from Union home minister Amit Shah over the police action against protesters, while simultaneously saying the opposition would not listen to him."I feel he is making a mockery of the country. He constantly ridicules the nation; for him, everything is a joke. This is the first time I am seeing Parliament being made such a mockery of. In the same breath, he says, 'We want an answer from Amit Shah ji--asking whether or not he did such-and-such to the students--while simultaneously declaring, 'We are not here to listen to him'. He has no sense of shame or propriety left," news agency ANI quoted Ranaut saying."The whole world is watching and wondering what kind of person this is. The way he is venting his frustration and insulting Parliament and, by extension, the entire nation and its citizens convinces me, as someone observing his role as leader of the opposition, that this will be his final term," she added.Ranaut, who represents Mandi in the Lok Sabha, also attacked Gandhi over his political record, saying the Congress under his leadership had "lost a hundred elections" and claiming that he would not retain the leader of opposition post in the future."He is demanding the resignation of the Prime Minister--a democratically elected leader who has secured a massive mandate for a third consecutive term. He seems to think that no one else in this country should even exist but him. Then there are his other actions--colluding with figures like Soros or international forces to tear the country apart and leave it in ruins. Ultimately, it doesn't matter whose resignation he demands or what he wants, because the public simply doesn't care about him," she said.The BJP MP's remarks came amid a continuing face-off between the government and the opposition over the July 20 student protests in Delhi. Opposition parties have been demanding a statement from Amit Shah over the alleged police action against protesters, leading to repeated adjournments. The Monsoon Session is set to end on Thursday.

Article Title: ‘Shortcuts will cut you short’: PM Modi’s message for youngsters at former President Kovind’s autobiography launch
Article Text:
Former President Ram Nath Kovind with PM Narendra Modi at book launch

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday urged youngsters to avoid taking shortcuts in life, warning that “a shortcut will cut you short.”He made the remarks while releasing the autobiography of former President Ram Nath Kovind in the national capital."I would particularly like to urge the younger generation—we live in the age of 'Reels' and social media influencers. Even in this era of shortcuts, let us remember something often written at railway stations: A shortcut will cut you short," PM Modi said.He also encouraged youngsters to read the autobiographies of personalities they admire, saying such accounts offer a unique perspective on the historic events of their time.“The period covered in a biography brings one very close to history itself. That is why I sincerely hope that the hard work put in by Kovind ji proves beneficial to future generations and especially to the youth,” PM Modi added.PM Modi further praised Kovind’s "guidance" and recalled the former president's “special affection and warmth” for him.“Today, we have the opportunity to witness the launch of Ramnath Kovind ji's autobiography.I have known Kovind ji for a very long time and have had the opportunity to know him closely. His guidance during his tenure as President, along with his special affection and warmth towards me, has been a truly valuable asset for me,” he said.Expressing confidence in the book’s significance, the prime minister described Kovind’s autobiography as a potential “cherished legacy” for Indian democracy and society.“... Based on my understanding of his life and my knowledge of his capabilities, I can say with full confidence that Ramnath Kovind ji's autobiography will become a cherished legacy for Indian democracy and society. There is so much I could speak about at length--regarding Kovind ji's life journey and his contributions to society and the nation. However, a book launch event should only serve as a 'curtain-raiser'; it is best if you all derive the full benefit of the book by reading it yourselves,” he added.Meanwhile, Kovind described the launch as an emotional moment and expressed gratitude to those who attended the event.“It is an emotional moment for me to address you all from this platform today. I have addressed you on several occasions, but today's occasion is different. I am grateful to all of you for joining this programme to mark the launch of my autobiography. I was wondering what I should say today. I have already written everything in my autobiography, and readers will read it,” the former president remarked.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi urges youngsters to avoid taking shortcuts in life. He made the remarks while releasing the autobiography of former President Ram Nath Kovind. PM Modi further praised Kovind’s "guidance" and recalled the former president's “special affection and warmth” for him.

Article Title: 'Not any individual, however big a name': Sunil Gavaskar's strong message ahead of Sri Lanka Tests
Article Text:
Indian cricket team (PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar has called for a shift in the way Indian cricket views success, urging the team and its supporters to put the interests of the collective ahead of individual stars.Gavaskar, who is currently in Singapore for the felicitation of India’s 1983 World Cup-winning team, believes the focus should remain on Indian cricket as a whole rather than being centred around “big” individuals.His comments come ahead of India’s opening Test against Sri Lanka in Galle, with the visitors facing a demanding task in their bid to reach the World Test Championship (WTC) final at The Oval next year.India’s defeat against South Africa last year has left them needing to win seven of their remaining nine Tests to stay in contention for a place in the WTC summit clash.Gavaskar, however, believes India are capable of beating Sri Lanka 2-0 in the two-Test series, provided the side has the confidence to do so. For him, that belief must be rooted in putting Indian cricket first."The two-match series in Sri Lanka won’t be easy, as Sri Lanka at home are a formidable team. Winning both these Tests would be a good start to the new Test season, as well as give the team the impetus it needs to qualify for the WTC Final," Gavaskar wrote in his column for Sportstar."To be able to do so requires loads of effort and also some luck, but, above all, the belief that Indian cricket should be the priority and not any individual, however big a name he may be," he added.Gavaskar’s call for a team-first approach comes at a time when Indian cricket has repeatedly debated its relationship with superstar culture. Current India head coach Gautam Gambhir has also been vocal about wanting the entire team to receive recognition rather than allowing the spotlight to remain concentrated on one or two high-profile players.India head into the Galle Test after a three-day practice match against SLC XI, which they won by six wickets. Devdutt Padikkal was the standout performer in the game, scoring an unbeaten century in the first innings.While discussing Indian cricket, Gavaskar also highlighted the influence of the Indian Premier League (IPL), describing it as an example of what a well-run competition can achieve.He pointed out that the success of the IPL has encouraged Indian franchise owners to invest in leagues overseas, contributing to the development of cricket ecosystems in other countries."Today, the IPL has shown the world what a well-organised tournament can do. The fruits of that success have spurred Indian franchise owners to venture into other countries and lift those countries’ cricketing ecosystems to a higher level than might otherwise have been possible," wrote Gavaskar.
Article Summary: Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar has called for a shift in the way Indian cricket views success. He has urged the team and its supporters to put the interests of the collective ahead of individual stars. His comments come ahead of India’s opening Test against Sri Lanka in Galle.

Article Title: Was Jamal really behind the deletion of IShowSpeed and Kai Cenat’s Minecraft Hardcore world? Viral clip explained
Article Text:
Was Jamal really behind the deletion of IShowSpeed and Kai Cenat’s Minecraft Hardcore world? Viral clip explained

Did Jamal delete IShowSpeed and Kai Cenat’s Minecraft Hardcore world?

IShowSpeed and Kai Cenat’s Minecraft Hardcore run continues

A viral clip from IShowSpeed’s Minecraft Hardcore stream made it look like his brother Jamal had erased the world he and Kai Cenat had spent hours building. That is not what happened. Jamal did delete a saved world while using Speed’s computer, but it was not the active Hardcore world. IShowSpeed later checked the clip himself and confirmed that the world he and Kai were using was still safe.The scare happened after IShowSpeed and Kai Cenat had made their best progress yet in the second edition of their Minecraft Hardcore challenge. On August 11, the pair had full enchanted diamond armor and several Totems of Undying, and they were preparing to face the Warden. They decided to stop for the night after a long session.While Speed was away, Jamal took control of the stream for a short time. He opened the “Select World” menu and clicked on the first saved world, which was named “???.” He then deleted it. Realizing what he had done, Jamal immediately reacted, saying, “Wait! Did I just delete their… No!”That was enough to make the chat fill with “Ls,” as viewers thought the duo had lost their progress.The current save had more than 20 hours of work behind it.Speed later woke up and saw messages telling him Jamal had deleted the world. Once he reached his setup, he watched the clip and checked the name of the active save. His reaction made the situation clear.“He didn’t delete ours. Chat, he didn’t delete ours. Bro, he was close. Nah, ours is [named ‘i got a bad b boat’]… Oh my god, I got scared for a minute.”So, the viral clip shows Jamal deleting a world, but not the one being used for the current Hardcore run. The active save is titled “i got a bad b boat.”The duo’s current challenge is the second edition of their Minecraft Hardcore journey. In their earlier run, they eventually defeated the Ender Dragon after more than 100 hours of gameplay. This time, their goal is bigger, with the Warden, Elder Guardian, Ender Dragon and Wither on their list.As of the latest update, Speed and Kai are on day six of the run and have recorded 42 deaths. Polymarket also listed the death count at 42. IShowSpeed has taken most of those falls. They are now preparing for the Warden, a powerful Minecraft mob with 500 health points, or 250 hearts, and very high attack damage.Their plan is to use their enchanted diamond armor, Iron Golems and Totems of Undying to survive the fight. A Totem can save a player from death when it is held in the correct hand and activated at the right moment.The earlier 2024 run ended with 42 deaths before the pair beat the Ender Dragon, according to Complex. The current challenge is still going, with another major fight ahead for the pair.
Article Summary: IShowSpeed and Kai Cenat had made their best progress yet in their Minecraft Hardcore challenge. Jamal took control of the stream for a short time and deleted a saved world. IShowSpeed later checked the clip himself and confirmed that the world he and Kai were using was still safe.

Article Title: Ryan Lochte marriage controversy deepens as ex wife Kayla Reid reveals alleged cheating, drug use and painful divorce battle
Article Text:
Ryan Lochte marriage controversy deepens as ex wife Kayla Reid reveals alleged cheating, drug use and painful divorce battle

Kayla Reid details Ryan Lochte marriage problems

Ryan Lochte and Kayla Reid divorce battle ends

Kayla Reid has spoken publicly about her divorce from Olympic swimmer Ryan Lochte, describing their eight-year marriage as a “ticking time bomb.” In a new PEOPLE interview published after their divorce was finalized, Reid, 35, said she faced repeated infidelity, drug use and lies that slowly changed how she saw their relationship. She also described a difficult final period before filing for divorce in January 2025.Reid said she had doubts about the marriage years before it ended, even writing in her journal that it felt like a “ticking time bomb.” She told PEOPLE, “I don’t think it was a love anyone deserved.”The couple met after Lochte contacted her on Instagram in 2016 and married in 2018 after welcoming their first child, Caiden.They later had two more children, Liv and Georgia. Reid said cheating became a serious problem early in the marriage.While she was pregnant with Caiden, she said she received photos showing Lochte close to another woman after he attended a wedding alone.She said he denied cheating, and she believed him at the time. Years later, while pregnant with Georgia, Reid said she found a revealing photo from another woman on Lochte’s phone.She said the discovery left her feeling guilty and ashamed, even though she believed she was the one being hurt.Reid also accused Lochte of using cocaine and nitrous oxide, saying she found evidence of cocaine use in Liv’s bedroom and saw nitrous oxide being used near their children.Lochte has acknowledged past drug use but denied using substances around his children. His recovery also became harder for the family after a 2023 crash left him with a broken femur. Reid said she became his main caregiver and also carried the family’s financial responsibilities.By January 2025, Reid said she had reached her limit. During a session with their therapist, she asked Lochte to enter a 30-day inpatient rehab program and then take part in marriage counseling.She said he refused, and she filed for divorce. The legal fight continued for more than a year before the divorce was finalized on July 1, 2026. According to TMZ, Reid received primary custody of their three children, while Lochte will pay $1,000 a month in child support.Lochte responded to the PEOPLE report by saying he has accepted responsibility for mistakes from his past and was not ready to be the husband and father his family needed.He also said any discussion about a confidentiality agreement was meant to protect his children, not his reputation. Lochte is now engaged to Molly Gillihan, who said she and the swimmer only reconnected after the divorce proceedings had already started.Reid, meanwhile, is focusing on real estate and her podcast, The Comeback Era. She said she now feels she has another chance at life and love. The settlement also leaves Reid with the Florida home, while Lochte has moved to Missouri for a college coaching job.
Article Summary: Kayla Reid, 35, said she faced repeated infidelity, drug use and lies that slowly changed how she saw their relationship. Reid said she had doubts about the marriage years before it ended, even writing in her journal that it felt like a “ticking time bomb.” The couple met after Lochte contacted her on Instagram in 2016 and married in 2018.

It could be in a year, or it could be in six months, or it could be in a month.”But it seems many fans are convinced by this fake narrative.A fan took to X and wrote, “That’s actually a pretty mature way to look at marriage…love can be genuine, but protecting yourself legally and financially doesn’t make the relationship any less real.”Another fan posted, “Finally the click came Respect to CR7 for protecting his bag and still making it official after all these years. Peak Twitter storytelling.”Another fan wrote, “This is totally false dude. Ronaldo mentioned the click but it has nothing to do with signing any prenup or Messi wading in and talking to his wife to persuade Georgina to sign anything. Always fact check what you post please.”Neither the former Manchester United star Cristiano Ronaldo nor his wife Georgina Rodriguez has commented on the fake rumors about their wedding yet.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “Without my mum I’d get too low with the lows or too high with the highs.” - How Jude Bellingham’s family turned small-town sacrifices into global football dominance
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “Without my mum I’d get too low with the lows or too high with the highs.” - How Jude Bellingham’s family turned small-town sacrifices into global football dominance

How did Mark Bellingham inspire Jude Bellingham’s love for football

How did Denise Bellingham support Jude Bellingham after his move to Germany

What did Jude Bellingham learn from Denise Bellingham away from football

Why do Jude Bellingham and Jobe Bellingham credit their parents

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jude Bellingham’s rise to the top of football has been backed by something much simpler than fame or money: his family. The Real Madrid and England star has repeatedly spoken about how his parents, Denise and Mark Bellingham, helped him handle the pressure that came with becoming a professional player at a young age. His father introduced him to football through his own non-league career, while his mother became a steady presence as Jude moved abroad. His younger brother, Jobe Bellingham, also followed the same football path, making the family’s journey closely linked to the sport.Before Jude Bellingham was playing in front of packed stadiums, he was watching his father play non-league football. Mark Bellingham worked as a police officer while also building a long career in the English non-league game. His football career included hundreds of goals, giving Jude an early look at what commitment to the sport meant.Those early weekends mattered to Jude. He did not first learn about football from the huge stages he would later reach. He watched his father play, saw the effort involved and slowly developed his own love for the game.Jude has explained that his father was his first football hero and that those matches helped shape his interest in the sport.“We talk about footballing heroes, and my dad was like my first. When you go and watch him play every week in non-league… seeing the way that he played and the atmosphere-it made me fall in love with football, so he was probably my first hero.”That connection also helps explain why Jude has often spoken about his childhood in simple terms. Football was part of family life long before it became his career.England Football has previously published Jude’s reflections on his early football years and his parents’ influence. He also said his father’s involvement in football played an important part in getting him interested in the game in the first place.Jude’s move from Birmingham City to Borussia Dortmund in 2020 changed his life quickly. He was only 17 when he left England for Germany, and his family had to find a way to support him without putting Jobe’s own football journey on hold.Denise moved to Germany with Jude. Mark stayed in England with Jobe, who was also working towards a professional football career. It meant the family had to spend long periods apart while both brothers followed their own paths.For Jude, having his mother nearby was about much more than everyday help. She gave him someone he could rely on while he adjusted to a new country, a new club and the demands of senior football.Jude has been very open about that role. He has said that Denise helped him stay level-headed when things were going well and when they were not.“The role my mum plays is massive. I think at the minute it is probably the biggest role of anyone, even probably more than my coaches and managers to be honest… Without my mum, sometimes I’d get too low with the lows or too high with the highs, and I stay pretty humble because I’ve got her around.”That support continued when Jude moved from Dortmund to Real Madrid in 2023. Denise moved to Spain with him, while Mark continued supporting Jobe as his younger son developed his own career.Jude’s comments about his mother show that her influence has not been limited to football. He has often linked what she taught him at home with the way he behaves on the pitch.For a player dealing with major matches, huge expectations and constant attention, keeping emotions under control can be as important as technical ability. Jude says Denise helped him build that side of his personality.“My mum’s kind of the backbone. She’s the one who gives me the support I need as a son, like emotionally and mentally… I have my mum who has taught me more about life outside football, but it merges quite well. And even some of the stuff that my mum has taught me, I do take it on to the pitch, about staying calm, staying cool, being a good example to my teammates.”There was also a lighter side to that relationship. During the 2022 World Cup, Jude spoke about how closely his mother watched his behaviour during matches.“My mum’s been telling me all week to watch my language, watch my tackles, watch my face, watch my emotions. So yeah, I think she drilled it into me all week about being careful.”It is a small detail, but it says a lot about their relationship. Even after Jude had become one of England’s biggest young stars, Denise was still the person reminding him about the basics.The Bellingham family story is not only about Jude. Jobe also became a professional footballer, meaning Denise and Mark had two sons trying to build careers in the same demanding sport.That made the family’s support a long-term commitment rather than something focused on one player. Mark and Denise had to balance the needs of both sons, sometimes from different countries, while allowing each of them to develop independently.Jude has said the values he learned from his parents mattered just as much as the football lessons he received.“Before being great parents, they’re great people. I’ve grown up around them and seen the way they interact with other people, seen the way they treat people. When you have people like that, you don’t have to be told how to behave, you pick that up from them. Both are working-class and filled me with the things you need to get along… not giving up, working hard and if you want something, putting in the graft to go and get it.”That attitude has remained a major part of how Jude talks about his success. He does not describe his rise only through goals, trophies or transfers. Instead, he repeatedly brings the conversation back to the people who helped him get there.The family also made practical sacrifices along the way. When Jude was travelling to training and matches as a young player, his parents spent long hours taking him where he needed to go. Those ordinary parts of childhood football became part of the foundation for the career that followed.Jude’s success has since reached the highest level. He became a Champions League winner with Real Madrid, established himself as an important England player and continued to develop into one of the most recognised young footballers in the world.Yet the story behind that rise remains rooted in Stourbridge, family support and the work his parents put in before the biggest stadiums knew his name.For Jude, that may be why his mother’s influence remains so important. Football can bring huge highs and difficult lows, but the people who knew him before the fame can give him a sense of normal life. In his own words, Denise helps him stay somewhere in the middle.That balance has become one of the most striking parts of Jude Bellingham’s story: a young footballer who reached the biggest stage while continuing to value the family that helped him get there.
Article Summary: Real Madrid and England star Jude Bellingham credits his parents for his success. His father, Mark, played non-league football and introduced him to the game. His mother, Denise, was a steady presence as Jude moved abroad. Jude has said that Denise helped him stay level-headed when things were going well.

Article Title: Will Jeanie Buss keep her Lakers role after record $12.5 billion ownership shake-up?
Article Text:
Jeanie Buss. Image via: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-USA TODAY Sports

Jeanie Buss' Lakers role revealed after $12.5 billion sale

How a Vegas expansion pitch turned into a $12.5 billion Lakers deal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jeanie Buss will remain governor of the Los Angeles Lakers even as the franchise changes hands again, this time in a record $12.5 billion sale from Mark Walter to an ownership group led by Bob Iger and Josh Kushner. The deal, reported Wednesday, comes just over a year after Walter bought the team from the Buss family for $10 billion.Iger confirmed to Khobi Price of the California Post that his group intends to honor the arrangement Walter made with Buss in that original sale, which guaranteed her the governor role for at least five years.Buss stepping away from day-to-day control of the Lakers seemed like a real possibility once word broke that Walter was selling. Instead, the incoming ownership group is keeping the arrangement Walter struck with the Buss family intact."We have enormous respect and appreciation for Jeanie, her father and what they've contributed to this franchise," Iger said. "And we have every intention to honor the agreement that was made between Mark and Jeanie. If things change, they'll change, but we're going into this with enormous respect and appreciation for who she is and what she represents in the organization."That last line matters. Iger isn't calling the arrangement permanent. He's calling it intact for now, with room to revisit it later.Iger and Kushner weren't shopping for the Lakers. They were chasing a different opportunity entirely, an ownership stake in the NBA's potential expansion franchise in Las Vegas, when Walter's willingness to sell reached them last weekend."We were involved in pursuing the new franchise in Vegas," Iger said. "And while that happened, it was suggested to us that maybe Mark Walter would be interested in selling his stake in the Lakers. And we immediately decided that given the value of the franchise and the iconic nature of the team, that we would be really smart to pursue it. The deal came together in three days.""It's that simple," he added.Three business days is a fast turnaround for a $12.5 billion transaction involving one of the NBA's flagship franchises, and Iger doesn't sound like someone still catching his breath from it."Grateful, appreciative, excited to own something that's as iconic as the LA Lakers," Iger said. "Josh and I are avid NBA fans. And to have an opportunity to own not just any NBA team, but the LA Lakers is…it's extraordinary from a life experience perspective and business perspective. It's still sinking in. We're very excited."Iger has already made two calls that matter. He's spoken with Buss, and he's spoken with head coach JJ Redick, a relationship that dates back to Redick's years with the Clippers from 2013 to 2017, when Iger held Clippers season tickets. One call he hasn't made yet stands out, Luka Doncic, the franchise's current star and the player any new ownership group needs on board.Iger isn't pretending to have the Lakers' future mapped out. He and Kushner went from pursuing an expansion team in Las Vegas to owning the Lakers in roughly 72 hours, and he said as much when asked what comes next, that no concrete plans exist yet beyond honoring what's already in place.For now, that means Jeanie Buss stays in her role, at least through the term Walter guaranteed her. Iger's own words leave the only real question hanging over the deal: how long "for now" actually lasts.
Article Summary: Bob Iger and Josh Kushner bought the Los Angeles Lakers for a record $12.5 billion. The deal comes just over a year after Mark Walter bought the team from the Buss family for $10 billion. Jeanie Buss will remain in her role as governor of the Lakers.

Article Title: Who was Michiel Vandeweert? Viral Belgian Twitch streamer who defied a 12-Year prognosis dies at 28
Article Text:
Who was Michiel Vandeweert? Viral Belgian Twitch streamer who defied a 12-Year prognosis dies at 28 (Instagram)

Who was Michiel Vandeweert? A look into his background and remarkable career

How did Michiel Vandeweert die?

Belgian Twitch streamer Michiel Vandeweert has died at the age of 28 after living with progeria, a rare genetic disorder that causes rapid aging. The news was confirmed in Belgium this week and quickly spread across social media, where thousands of followers remembered him for his humor, honesty, and positive outlook on life.What made Michiel’s story especially remarkable was that doctors had once believed he might live only until around the age of 12. Instead, he built a public career as a content creator, author, and gaming personality, becoming one of the most recognized people in Belgium living with progeria.Michiel Vandeweert was born in 1998 in Hasselt, in Belgium’s Limburg province, and grew up in the nearby town of Diepenbeek. He was diagnosed with Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome, an extremely rare genetic condition that affects only a small number of people worldwide. His parents, Godelieve and Wim Vandeweert, spent years searching for answers about his health before the diagnosis was confirmed.He came from a close-knit family and shared a strong bond with his younger sister, Amber Vandeweert, who was also diagnosed with progeria.The siblings later became the subject of public interest in Belgium because having two children with progeria in the same family is considered extraordinarily rare.Details about Michiel’s formal education have not been widely made public, but he often spoke about growing up feeling different from other children and facing bullying because of his appearance. Those experiences shaped much of his outlook on life and later influenced the way he connected with people online.Michiel eventually turned that openness into a career. He became known as a Twitch streamer, YouTuber, Instagram creator, and occasional DJ. His content mixed gaming, personal reflections, humor, and everyday moments from his life with progeria. He also wrote a memoir titled Ik Ben Michiel (“I Am Michiel”) when he was 15 years old, giving readers a candid look at his childhood and medical journey.One of the most memorable moments of his public career came in 2026, when he appeared alongside his sister in the documentary How To Be Alive: Amber and Michiel. The documentary introduced many viewers to his resilience and his ability to talk about a serious illness without losing his sense of humor. He also remained a passionate supporter of Belgian football club KRC Genk, which later paid tribute to him after his death.Michiel Vandeweert died on August 10 2026 at the age of 28. His death was confirmed by Flemish broadcaster VRT NWS through a statement from the production company connected to the documentary series in which he had recently appeared.The statement reads, "Michiel leaves a deep impression and an indelible memory with everyone who knew him or followed his story. We wish the parents, sister, family, and friends much strength during these difficult times.”The exact medical details were not fully disclosed publicly, but reports indicated that he had been dealing with serious complications related to progeria, particularly cardiovascular problems.Tributes poured in across Belgium after the announcement. Fans, fellow creators, local officials, and KRC Genk supporters remembered him not only as a streamer and influencer, but as someone who consistently encouraged others to appreciate life despite difficult circumstances.
Article Summary: Michiel Vandeweert was born in 1998 in Hasselt, in Belgium’s Limburg province. He was diagnosed with Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome, an extremely rare genetic condition that affects only a small number of people worldwide. He became known as a Twitch streamer, YouTuber, Instagram creator, and occasional DJ.

Article Text:

Russell Westbrook's basketball legacy of triple-doubles and gold medals

Russell Westbrook. Image via: Getty Images

Russell Westbrook. Image via: ANGELA WEISS/ AFP via Getty Images

Russell Westbrook is a man of a golden heart

Russell Westbrook announces retirement

Russell Westbrook, the two-time Olympic gold medalist and 2017 NBA MVP, announced his retirement from professional basketball on Wednesday, closing an 18-year career built on relentless energy and a refusal to be told what he couldn't do. He shared the news on X, writing, "Sometimes you don't even know when you've already watched the end. "The announcement ends a run that took Westbrook through seven franchises, including both hometown teams, the Los Angeles Lakers and Clippers. He finishes 14th on the NBA's all-time scoring list and fifth in assists, a resume built on triple-doubles, tunnel-walk fashion statements and a community footprint that outlasted every box score. Here’s the incredible story of NBA legend Russell Westbrook.Russell Westbrook was born in Long Beach and raised in Hawthorne, a crowded stretch of Los Angeles's South Bay where staying on track required more than talent. His parents kept him close to basketball, and basketball kept him out of trouble. He attended Leuzinger High School in Lawndale, an honor student who says he was accepted to Stanford with an academic scholarship but that tuition still ran too steep for his family.Physically, Westbrook was a late bloomer. As a junior he stood 5-foot-8 and couldn't dunk. He grew five inches the following summer, and by his senior year he was putting up 25.1 points and 8.7 rebounds a game, dragging Leuzinger to a 25-4 record and catching the attention of UCLA coach Ben Howland.At UCLA, Westbrook spent his freshman season fighting for minutes before breaking out as a sophomore, earning Pac-10 Defensive Player of the Year honors. He declared for the draft after two seasons, and the Seattle SuperSonics took him fourth overall in 2008. Analysts at the time called it a reach, arguing he needed more seasoning with the Bruins.Even away from campus, Westbrook carried the habits of a kid who had to earn everything. He is famously early to every team obligation, sometimes by two or three hours. Thunder general manager Sam Presti has told the story of showing up 30 minutes ahead of a pre-draft workout only to find Westbrook already waiting in the parking lot. Family stayed central throughout. In a 2015 interview with CBS Sunday Morning, Westbrook said he called his parents "before every game," adding, "Sometimes it may not be about basketball, sometimes it just may be about random things. "That early doubt, about his size, his recruiting stock, his readiness for the league, became the foundation of everything that followed. Westbrook built a career answering it the only way he knew how: by playing like the outcome was never decided.Westbrook's signature achievement arrived during the 2016-17 season with the Oklahoma City Thunder, when he averaged a triple-double across an entire year and won NBA MVP. He set the single-season triple-double record with 42, a number matched only by Oscar Robertson and Nikola Jokić. He averaged a triple-double in four separate seasons and once strung together 11 straight triple-doubles between January and February of 2019.By May 2021, Westbrook had passed Robertson's career triple-double mark altogether. He finished with 209, an NBA record. Along the way he collected nine All-NBA selections, two scoring titles, three assist titles and two All-Star Game MVPs, and he was named to the league's 75th Anniversary Team. He retires 14th in career scoring with 27,176 points and fifth in assists with 10,351.The international résumé matches the domestic one. Westbrook helped the United States win gold at the 2010 FIBA World Cup, then did it again at the 2012 London Olympics, where Team USA went 8-0 and beat Spain 107-100 in the final. He averaged 10.4 points, 2.4 rebounds and 2.4 assists in just over 16 minutes a game in London, with his defensive pressure, 1.2 steals a night, doing as much damage as his scoring.None of it changed the way Westbrook approached the sport. He treated every possession like it might be his last real chance to prove something, a mindset that made him equally beloved and, at times, criticized for playing with the same intensity whether it was game one or game 82.Westbrook's tunnel walks turned NBA arrivals into runway moments long before it became standard practice around the league. In a joint GQ interview with longtime friend James Harden, Westbrook framed the whole approach as a matter of conviction rather than costume. "You're passionate about something, I'm passionate about something," he said, adding that fashion is something he takes as seriously as anyone takes their own craft.The two, who met as kids playing in the same L.A. youth basketball circuit, spent much of the interview needling each other over spending habits, with Westbrook guessing Harden drops "$500K" a year on clothes. Harden pushed back on the public read of his friend, saying people mistake Westbrook's on-court intensity for his personality off it. "He's a pretty chill, cool guy," Harden said, adding that Westbrook is close with a small circle of friends he's had since high school.Westbrook himself has said he doesn't think most people understand him, describing repeated moments meeting business owners and designers who were surprised to learn who he was. He has also connected the sport of dressing to something more analytical than intuitive, once comparing picking an outfit to solving a math problem, fitting for a former honor student whose favorite subject was math.Away from the cameras and the closet, Westbrook built one of the more substantial philanthropic footprints of his generation. He founded the Russell Westbrook Why Not? Foundation in 2012, focused on education, workforce development and mental health access in underserved communities, and later opened "Russell's Reading Rooms" in Oklahoma City public schools. In 2021 he launched the Why Not? Academy with the LA Promise Fund, a school for middle and high schoolers that Westbrook says posted a 100 percent graduation rate last year.He has stayed hands-on rather than simply writing checks. After tornadoes tore through Moore, Oklahoma, in May 2013, Westbrook, still recovering from knee surgery, called the Thunder's PR staff and told them to "get me out there with the people," then showed up on crutches to encourage residents in a devastated neighborhood.Westbrook has been direct about why the work matters to him. "It all stems from community and impact, and that is the focal point of everything," he said in a CNN feature, explaining the name behind his foundation. "Why not us? Why not you? Why not me to be able to do great things."Westbrook's final chapter closes with the city that raised him still very much on his mind. He has spoken with visible excitement about Los Angeles hosting the 2028 Olympics, with basketball set for the Intuit Dome near where he once lived. "The city, this arena, the people. It's going to be exciting for L.A.," he said, "especially being a local."For a player who spent nearly two decades proving people wrong about what an undersized, three-star recruit from Hawthorne could become, the final word belonged to him alone. "You had to be there," Westbrook wrote in his announcement.
Article Summary: Russell Westbrook announced his retirement from professional basketball on Wednesday. The announcement ends an 18-year career built on relentless energy and a refusal to be told what he couldn't do. He finishes 14th on the NBA's all- time scoring list and fifth in assists.

What happens next for the Lakers

Jeanie Buss needed only two words to back Luka Doncic after the Lakers' second ownership change in under two years. She replied to his statement on X, adding purple and gold heart emojis, after news broke that Josh Kushner and Bob Iger have agreed to buy the franchise at a $12.5 billion valuation.The pending sale arrives about 14 months after Mark Walter took controlling interest from the Buss family at a $10 billion valuation, and just weeks after LeBron James left for the Philadelphia 76ers. That leaves Doncic as the unquestioned face of the franchise during its third ownership transition since he arrived in Los Angeles.Jeanie Buss shared, “Perfectly said 💛💜.” It was a short reply by design. Rather than address the uncertainty around another change at the top, she chose to amplify Doncic's own words about staying committed to the franchise. "Being a Laker means everything to me," Doncic wrote, adding that he's gotten used to upheaval over the past few years but still sees no ceiling on what the organization can become. He said he's looking forward to meeting Kushner and Iger to start building toward a title together.He added, “And I’m excited to get back on the court and bring a championship to LA. I’ve gotten used to big changes over these last few years, but I know that no matter what, there is no limit to the potential of this iconic franchise.I look forward to meeting Josh and Bob so we can get to work building something special in LA together.”Buss, who was central to trading for Doncic in February 2025 and to signing him to a three-year, $165 million extension that August.Variety confirmed the agreement, which still requires Thrive Capital's due diligence and NBA approval before it closes. Kushner, who also holds a minority stake in the Miami Heat, and Iger, the former Disney CEO now advising Thrive, framed the purchase as a continuation rather than a break from the past. "We have immense respect for the leadership and vision of Jerry and Jeanie Buss," they said in a joint statement, pledging to build on that foundation and serve the team, its fans and Los Angeles.The Buss family will keep a minority stake, preserving a link to the franchise that dates to Jerry Buss' 1979 purchase. The Los Angeles Times has reported Jeanie Buss is expected to stay on as governor for at least five years, though the full front-office structure under the incoming owners hasn't been spelled out.Whether Kushner and Iger eventually reshape the front office Walter rebuilt remains unanswered, and Buss didn't address it Wednesday. What she did settle, in six words, was where the franchise's most important player stands.Doncic wants a championship in Los Angeles and a seat at the table with the new owners.

Kolkata Knight Riders have added to the buzz around Hardik Pandya's IPL future after posting a video featuring the Mumbai Indians captain. Article Title: Are the Jonas Brothers headlining the Super Bowl? NFL's Melbourne halftime news has fans confused and frustrated
Article Text:
Jonas Brothers to headline NFL's first-ever Australia game as 49ers, Rams make history in Melbourne

"I thought this was the Super Bowl": Fans got confused as Jonas Brothers headline NFL's first-ever Australia game

No, they are not performing for the Superbowl

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The NFL 's announcement that the Jonas Brothers will headline the halftime show at the league's first-ever game in Australia didn't land the way the league might have hoped. Within hours of the news breaking, football fans flooded social media with reactions ranging from confusion to outright frustration. Some mistook the announcement for Super Bowl halftime news, others venting about ticket prices, the NFL's growing international slate, and whether football needs a pop concert attached to it at all. What was meant to be a celebratory moment for the league's biggest global expansion yet instead became a flashpoint for fans already skeptical of the NFL's overseas ambitions.The most common reaction wasn't about the band at all, it was about scale. Multiple fans admitted they briefly assumed the Jonas Brothers had been booked for the actual Super Bowl halftime show, with several saying they nearly panicked before realizing this was a regular-season international game instead.One user joked they were seconds away from missing the Puppy Bowl over the confusion. The mix-up says as much about how big international games have become in the NFL's marketing push as it does about the band itself, casual scrollers are struggling to tell a Week 1 Melbourne matchup apart from the league's biggest night.The Melbourne performance isn't just another halftime show, it's the opening act of the NFL's biggest international push yet. This is the first of a record seven halftime shows presented across the league's 2026 International Games, a slate that spans seven countries and four continents, making it the most globally ambitious season in NFL history.The Jonas Brothers, who've sold more than 20 million albums and built a multi-generational fanbase, were an easy pick for the league's entertainment team, who called them "global entertainers whose music connects across generations." There's also a neat bit of trivia fueling the buzz: "Australia" happens to be a track off the band's own 2007 sophomore album, a coincidence the brothers themselves pointed out in their statement announcing the gig.The Rams-49ers matchup carries weight well beyond the halftime entertainment. It marks the NFL's first regular-season game on Australian soil, part of a nine-game international slate spanning seven countries this season, the most the league has ever played outside U.S.borders in a single year.The game is being staged in partnership with the Victorian State Government and Visit Victoria, and will anchor a full weekend of festivities, including the NFL Kickoff Festival running September 10 through 12 at Melbourne Park, featuring local Australian acts.For the 49ers, Melbourne is just the first stop on an international tour, the team is also set to play in Mexico City on November 22 against the Minnesota Vikings, making this the franchise's most globally active season yet. With more international halftime performers still to be announced in the coming weeks, the Jonas Brothers' Melbourne set is shaping up to be the loud, unmistakable kickoff to the NFL's most ambitious global year on record.

Fans flooded social media with reactions ranging from confusion to outright frustration. Article Title: A father's race against time: Ex-NFL running back Wendell Smallwood released from prison to be with his dying 8-year-old daughter
Article Text:
Wendell Smallwood

Ex-NFL running back granted early release as his 8-year-old daughter battles terminal cancer

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Some fights can't be won in a courtroom, and Wendell Smallwood Jr. knows that better than anyone right now. The former NFL running back, who spent three seasons carrying the ball for the Philadelphia Eagles and was part of their Super Bowl LII championship roster, has spent the last several months behind bars for a COVID-era fraud case that has nothing to do with football and everything to do with a chapter of his life he's said he takes full responsibility for. But none of that mattered on August 7, when a New Jersey courtroom filled with his family, all of them praying for the same thing: that a judge would let him out in time to hold his daughter one more time.Mila Smallwood is eight years old. Earlier this year, she was diagnosed with diffuse anaplastic Wilms tumor, a rare and aggressive form of childhood kidney cancer. Her family did everything they could, round after round of chemotherapy, but the disease didn't respond.Doctors have since moved her into palliative care, telling the family there's nothing left to do but keep her comfortable. She has, by medical estimates, days to weeks left to live. For any parent, that sentence alone is unbearable. For Wendell Smallwood, it came with the added agony of watching it unfold from behind bars, unsure if he'd be free in time to say goodbye.Smallwood was serving an 18-month federal sentence for a fraud scheme tied to COVID-19 relief programs, a case he pleaded guilty to in late 2024.He was also facing a separate state charge in New Jersey for possessing an assault rifle, one that legally could have kept him incarcerated well into November, long after Mila's doctors expect she'll be gone.That changed when a federal appeals court struck down New Jersey's assault weapons ban in July, opening a narrow legal path for Smallwood to withdraw his plea. His attorney, Yaron Helmer, stood before Judge Renard Scott and made the only argument that mattered: this wasn't about legal technicalities anymore; it was about whether a little girl would get to hold her father again.The judge agreed. Citing Mila's illness as an untreatable, time-sensitive circumstance, Scott granted the motion, denying prosecutors' request to delay the ruling. Smallwood was expected to walk free as early as August 10.In the middle of the legal relief, Smallwood's wife, Autumn, made clear the family isn't celebrating, they're bracing. In a brief statement, she thanked those following the case for their support but was careful to keep the focus where it belongs.Their fight, she said, was never really about the courtroom. It was, and still is, about their daughter. She asked people to keep Mila in their prayers as she continues to fight for every day she has left.There's no version of this story with a happy ending, only a slightly less painful one. A father who gets to be present, instead of absent, for whatever time remains. Naomi Osaka has long been known for making a statement with her tennis. Now, her influence is reaching well beyond the baseline. The four-time Grand Slam champion says fashion has introduced her to a new audience and pushed her outside her comfort zone. As Osaka prepares for another North American hard-court swing, her evolving identity is becoming an important part of her story.Osaka has never treated fashion as an afterthought. Her Grand Slam appearances have often featured carefully chosen looks that reflect her personality, culture and creativity. That visibility has now helped her connect with people who may not follow tennis closely.Speaking during the 2026 DC Open, Osaka admitted that her fashion profile has started attracting a different kind of audience."Then people are knowing me now for the fashion stuff more than the tennis, like fashion enthusiasts more than tennis fans," Osaka said.For a player who has openly described herself as an introvert, that shift has brought an unexpected challenge. Fashion has placed Osaka in rooms and conversations she may not have entered through tennis alone."Doing the fashion stuff has made me talk to people that I've never met before and things like that.I'm just trying to go into worlds that I've never imagined myself sort of being in before."That willingness to explore unfamiliar spaces says plenty about where Osaka is in her career. She is no longer simply presenting herself as an athlete. Her interests have expanded, and fashion has become one of the clearest ways she expresses that broader identity.It also gives fans a different way to understand her. Tennis can reveal Osaka's competitiveness and discipline, but her fashion choices allow more room for creativity and personality.The crossover has worked both ways. Fashion fans are discovering Osaka, while the tennis star is gaining experiences and connections outside her usual sporting circle.While fashion has given Osaka a fresh platform, her competitive ambitions remain firmly intact.Her 2026 Wimbledon campaign ended in the quarterfinals after she lost to Karolina Muchova in straight sets. Reaching the last eight represented a strong run, but Osaka admitted that she struggled emotionally with the result because she believed she had an opportunity to go even further."Maybe for like a couple of days or so, I was just really disappointed in myself," Osaka said. Those results raised expectations heading into another crucial stretch of the calendar.At the 2026 DC Open, Osaka entered as the third seed and received a first-round bye. She is set to face either Katie Boulter or wildcard Ashlyn Krueger in the second round.For Osaka, the weeks ahead offer more than a chance to improve her ranking. They provide an opportunity to show that her fashion-forward identity and her tennis ambitions can coexist.She may be attracting new fans through her style, but the competitive fire that made her a four-time Grand Slam champion remains the heart of her story.
